- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope after peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates future gains; cap forecast at 1.2x recent high or use moving average of last 5 days for smoothing.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.25) and price is near recent mean, model exhibits lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates mean reversion in low-sentiment periods; add 2–3% upward bias to forecast if sentiment <0.4 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is rising (increasing >0.1 per day) and price is falling, model underestimates reversal; add 3–5% upward bias to forecast to capture sentiment-driven bounce.
